description: Patch releases of the Anki synchronization server are automerged here. This role hosts data - one SQLite collection per user under `anki_data_path` - so the question that decides it is whether a newer server rewrites a collection an older one wrote, and whether that is one-way. Measured rather than assumed: a collection created by 25.09.4 and then served by 26.08 keeps the same schema timestamp (`scm` in the sync metadata) and the same bytes on disk, and is afterwards still read by 25.09.4 and even by 23.10.1, the oldest tag the image publishes. That is the Typesense shape rather than the Meilisearch one - nothing here refuses data written by another version.

That matches the upstream code. Anki's collection schema is pinned at `SCHEMA_MAX_VERSION = 18` in rslib/src/storage/upgrades/mod.rs and has been since 2021; that directory has not had a functional change since February 2023. Seven patch spans were compared file by file - 25.02...25.02.1, 25.02.6...25.02.7, 25.07...25.07.1, 25.07.4...25.07.5, 25.09...25.09.2, 25.09.3...25.09.4 and 26.08...26.08.1 - and only the first touches rslib/src/storage or rslib/src/sync at all: a rusqlite closure cleanup, and a new field carrying the collection's size so that oversized collections can be rejected. No migration and no schema change in any of them. Minor and major bumps, which is where Anki does move things, remain human-reviewed pull requests.

The automerge branch is covered by the Molecule run, which does more than watch the unit turn active - `Restart=always` would keep a crash-looping container's unit active anyway, and the server's `/health` handler returns 200 for any instance whatever its configuration says. The `default` scenario speaks the sync protocol instead: it logs in with the configured credentials and gets a sync key, is refused with 403 for a wrong password, an unknown user and a forged key, fetches collection metadata, and then finds the collection the server created as an SQLite database under the role's data path. The `upgrade` scenario installs an older release, syncs against it, upgrades to the pinned one and asserts the collection is still served with its schema timestamp intact, then rolls back to the older release and asserts that it still reads the collection. A patch bump that broke startup, the credentials, the protocol or the stored collections fails there before it can merge.

`versioning=loose` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what makes any of this reachable. The image carries Anki's own version numbers, which have two components until a release gets its first patch (26.05, 26.08) and three afterwards (26.08.1, 25.09.4). Under Renovate's default `docker` versioning a two-component pin only ever sees two-component tags: running Renovate against this repository reported no updates whatsoever for `26.08` while 26.08.1 was already published, and offered `26.05` only `26.08`. With loose versioning the same lookup reports `26.08` -> `26.08.1` as the patch update it is.
